title: Telecom-compatible polarization-to-time-bin conversion of atom-photon entanglement for heterogeneous quantum networks
authors: Christian Haen, Julian Groß-Funk, Max Bergerhoff, Pascal Baumgart, Jonas Meiers, Tobias Bauer, Christoph Becher, Jürgen Eschner
abstract: A key enabling feature of future quantum networks is interoperability between platforms that operate at different wavelengths and with different qubit encodings. We demonstrate an interface that converts atom-photon entanglement from polarization encoding at an atomic wavelength to time-bin encoding in the telecom C-band. Atom-entangled photons at 854 nm are generated from a single $^{40}$Ca$^+$ ion. After quantum frequency conversion to 1550 nm, the photonic polarization qubit is converted into a time-bin qubit using a fiber-based Mach--Zehnder-like encoder. Full quantum tomography of the final state verifies that the process preserves entanglement with 96.3(4.2)% fidelity. Together with the independent work of Ferrari et al. [arXiv:2607.07805 (2026)], this is the first demonstration of polarization-to-time-bin conversion of photons entangled with a single atomic quantum memory. The telecom-compatible interface enables robust qubit transmission over optical fibers and provides a key building block for heterogeneous quantum networking architectures.
summary: The paper presents an experimental demonstration of converting atom-photon entanglement from polarization encoding at 854 nm to time-bin encoding at the telecom C-band (1550 nm). This conversion is achieved via Quantum Frequency Conversion and a specialized fiber encoder. The success provides a vital, high-fidelity building block necessary for realizing complex, heterogeneous quantum network architectures.
main_problem: The core challenge is creating an interoperable interface for quantum networks by converting atom-photon entanglement from polarization encoding at atomic wavelengths to time-bin encoding in the telecom C-band.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated this conversion, preserving entanglement with high fidelity (96.3% reported), establishing a crucial building block for heterogeneous quantum networking architectures.
method: The process involves generating polarization-entangled photons from a trapped ion, performing Quantum Frequency Conversion (QFC) to the telecom band, and finally using a fiber-based Mach–Zehnder-like encoder to map the qubit basis from polarization to time-bin.
model_or_system: The system utilizes a single $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ion trapped in a Paul trap for entanglement generation. The photonic qubits are manipulated through QFC and then encoded into time-bins using an unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer over optical fibers.
key_observables: Process fidelity (e.g., 96.3% reported), quantum state tomography results, and the measured photon wave-packets.
important_parameters: Atomic wavelength (854 nm) vs. Telecom C-band (1550 nm); time delay ($\sim 90$ ns) associated with the time-bin encoding path difference ($\Delta L \approx 18$ m).
main_assumptions: The process assumes that time-bin qubits are more robust than polarization qubits over long fiber links, and fidelity losses are attributed to component inefficiencies.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the entire interface connecting components like Paul traps, QFCs, TBEs, and APC systems. Tomography figures show density matrices ($ho$) for both encoding types alongside measured fidelities.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, starting with entanglement generation at an atomic wavelength, followed by quantum frequency conversion to the telecom band, and concluding with the polarization-to-time-bin conversion using a time-bin encoder. Stability analysis and fidelity verification are key components.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a major engineering hurdle in quantum networking—interoperability between different physical platforms (e.g., atomic memories vs. fiber links) by providing a high-fidelity quantum interface.
